newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes show short term strength.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes show short term strength.

text.p: North Sea crudes showed some strength on Tuesday but traders felt that this would be short lived with most of the buying now covered and refining margins not very healthy.
"The first decade (of February) looks well supported but after that it looks black," one commented.
Three cargoes of Brent crude traded on Tuesday. A Feb 4-6 loader at March Brent +28 cents was later sold on at an undisclosed price, thought Dated related.
A Feb 2-4 cargo was sold by a trader to a P+C buyer, again the price was heard Dated Brent related.
Both Brent cargoes were kept on Tuesday and, with one expected to be part of a VLCC to the U.S., traders saw only one Brent cargo left for sale - a Feb 5-7.
"But that VLCC has taken all the U.S. buying out of the market and the (refining) margins are not great so it does look bearish in the longer (2-3 week) term," a North Sea equity holder said.
It was not clear yet if the problems at Grangemouth and Kinneil would result in loading delays on Forties.
"If they do they will be minimal," one regular Forties buyer said.

BP said on Tuesday its 180,000 bpd Grangemouth refinery was restarting operations after a power failure closed the plant on Monday afternoon. The nearby Kinneil separation plant was also being returned to service.

With the Ekofisk field now back in production, equity holders expected the revised January programme to be announced early on Wednesday, followed by the delayed February programme later on Wednesday or early Thursday.
Other North Sea wet action included three Oseberg cargoes and one Draugen with full details not available.
The Brent Feb/Mar came off a high around +37 cents to talk around +33 cents in late action, reflecting a more bearish feel on the market, traders said.
The Mediterranean sour crude market was drawing support from a narrow differential between high and low sulphur fuel oil.
"Low sulphur fuel oil is very weak... the spread is narrowing...so all sour grades are attractive," said one trader.
Russian Urals was also bolstered by supply disruptions at the main Black Sea oil port of Novorossiisk, traders said.
Novorossiisk has been shut since 2330 local time on Saturday due to a heavy swell, shipping sources said.
Urals was last reported traded at Dated Brent -78 cents, but traders expected next offers to be around the Dated Brent -70 cents level.
Competition from Iraqi Kirkuk crude was expected to cap gains, but traders said that Urals differentials could go up to Dated Brent -65/60 cents and still be attractive against Kirkuk.
"People want to sell (Kirkuk) with a premium (to the Iraqi asking price of Dated Brent -$1.55), and in that case Urals still looks better for refiners," a Med refiner said.
An 80,000 tonne Kirkuk cargo was fixed by a European major on Tuesday to load at the Turkish port of Ceyhan on Jan 26 for delivery into the Med or the U.K., shipping sources said.
